address: Stadhouderskade 111 / Tweede Jan van der Heijdenstraat, Amsterdam-Zuid (De Pijp): 1872 block of dark painted brick shopfront rows, a red-brick factory-style wing with cream window bands and a 1950s balcony block round a supermarket yard
notes: Stadhouderskade 111 (BAG, built 1872) is the De Pijp block round the Albert Heijn/Blokker yard between Stadhouderskade and Tweede Jan van der Heijdenstraat; 359 3DBAG wall surfaces, many party walls. Photographed fronts: w01-6 (north street run, 2021-04-26), w02-155 (the SE brick wing, 2021-04-23), w03-186 (the supermarket gate with the 1950s brick block, 2021-04-23). w04-6 and w05-186 are close-ups of the same fronts. Everything else stays blank (otherWalls).

walls[0] and walls[1] = the north run on the street, two sets of 3DBAG surfaces of the 14.5-15 m row-house fronts (surfaces 83, 95, 165, 166, 183 and 130, 185, 202, 352, 353): dark painted brick, cream window surrounds and cornice, glazed shopfronts. Drawn as 4 storeys, 5 and 4 bays, plain windows, a plinth-shopfront ground, cornice and string courses. The other row-house surfaces (12.2-13.7 m) and the differing rooflines are left blank/3DBAG roof; the individual gables and house-by-house colour changes are not modelled.

walls[2] = surface 104 of panel 8: the red-brick wing, 4 storeys x 9 bays of cross windows with cream string courses. walls[3] = surface 55 of panel 47: the 1950s block beside the Albert Heijn gate, a grey tiled base, 4 storeys of paired windows and a stack of balconies at the right-hand bay; drawn as 5 storeys x 3 bays with a bar balcony on storeys 2-4 of bay 2. Simplified: the tenant fascias (Albert Heijn, Blokker), the red doors, the tiled base colour; the Albert Heijn entrance gate itself is outside this pand.
Not drawn: the courts, the south-east low supermarket wall (panel 47 surfaces 121 and 225, 4.6 m) and the party walls.

walls[2] = surfaces 185 and 202 of the north run, split out of walls[1]: that 5.7 m panel has its eaves at 12.06 m with a gable above, while the 4-storey grid of walls[1] put a 2.1 m window (11.93-14.02 m) across the eaves into the gable, flush with its brick (2.6 m2 coplanar glass against brick at 13.6, 13.0, -30.0). Drawn as 3 storeys x 2 bays so the windows stay below the eaves.

Uninstalled 2026-10-14 (likeness triage, plan Part 1 lane D): an 1872 row of individually different brown-brick and buff houses (each crop shows several distinct fronts with balconies and ornamented heads) was drawn as one dark painted grid and one red grid; ride-visible (50 of 2,000 sampled routes). Irregular row: uninstalled; belongs to the per-house block-face tier.
